articles.title: Budget 2026: Key points at a glance
articles.description: Here’s what you need to know from John Healey’s first Budget, as the chancellor sets out the government’s tax and spending plans.
articles.summary: Chancellor John Healey has set out the government's tax and spending plans in his Budget – the first since Andy Burnham became prime minister.

articles.title: The one thing that didn't change that will affect your pay the most
articles.description: The point at which you start to pay tax, and the point where you tip into paying a higher rate of tax have been frozen for three more years.
articles.summary: Income tax thresholds, which have been frozen under successive chancellors, will stay at current levels until April 2031 as planned.
key_points: But after that they are expected to start to rise again with inflation.
John Healey may not have mentioned the end of this policy in his Budget speech - after all, it is still some way off - but according to the documents released by the…
The proportion of your income that is taken in tax will continue to go up over the next four years in line with decisions made in previous Budgets.

articles.title: Your pay, energy bills and savings: How the Budget affects you
articles.description: Changes announced by Chancellor John Healey in his first Budget will affect your finances directly. Here's how.
articles.summary: Families facing cost-of-living pressures are being offered some help, or "breathing space" as Chancellor John Healey is calling it.
key_points: The help comes as prices are rising faster than expected with annual energy bills in particular likely to increase by hundreds of pounds in January.
Here's how the key announcements in the Budget affect you and your money.
If you are living in a home in council tax bands A to D in England, you will receive a one-off £100 "Household Energy Payment" from January, funded by extra tax on banks.

articles.title: Will I get the £100 energy payment and when will I receive it?
articles.description: Here is what you need to know about the payment that millions will receive from January.
articles.summary: Up to 20 million households in England will get a £100 payment directly into their bank accounts this winter, the government has announced.
key_points: For many people, the £100 on offer is a lot of money, but it's worth considering the context.
A typical yearly energy bill is forecast to jump by £276 in January , so many people will still feel worse off despite the payment.
Those living in properties which are in council tax bands A to D in England will get the payment, the government has said.

articles.title: How much is the minimum wage going up by?
articles.description: What are the National Minimum Wage and the National Living Wage, and how much are they worth?
articles.summary: The official minimum rates of pay will rise for 2.3 million workers on 1 April.
key_points: The rate for workers aged 21 and over is called the National Living Wage, while those aged 18 to 20 are paid the National Minimum Wage.
From 1 April 2027, workers over 21 on the National Living Wage will be paid £13.21p per hour, up 50p from the current £12.71 an hour.
For someone working full time (35 hours a week), that means an increase of £910 to their gross annual earnings, according to the Treasury.

articles.title: You may get the right to find out what your colleagues earn - here's why
articles.description: Employees should legally be able to find out what their co-workers are earning, the UK's equality watchdog says
articles.summary: Employees should legally be able to find out what their colleagues are earning, the UK's equality watchdog has said.
key_points: Bosses should be required to respond to questionaires about colleagues' pay to cut pay discrimination, the Equality and Human Rights Commission (EHRC) has proposed , external .
In addition, employers should be prevented from asking about current salary when offering a job to stop a history of discrimination from carrying on, it said.
Employers in the UK are currently allowed to ask you how much you get paid in your current role, but applicants are under no obligation to tell them .

articles.title: Luxury cruise passengers stranded in Cambodia due to soaring fuel costs
articles.description: The Villa Vie Odyssey suspended its voyage and is working with passengers on "temporary living arrangements".
articles.summary: The Villa Vie Odyssey was more than 750 days into its voyage around the world when it came to a stop in Cambodia A luxury cruise ship on a years-long voyage around the world said it suspended operations due to extraordinarily high fuel costs, leaving passengers stranded in Cambodia.
key_points: The US-based operator of Villa Vie Odyssey said it was working with passengers on disembarkation plans and "temporary living arrangements".
It is unclear how many were on board but the nearly 200m (656ft) vessel can carry up to 650 passengers.
It departed Belfast in October 2024 for a "continuous voyage around the world".
